PANCHO CARTER, 32, of Brownsburg, Ind., earned his
first career Indy Car win in last year's Norton-Michigan
500 at Brooklyn, Mich. and went on to finish third on the

JOHNNY RUTHERFORD, 44, of Fort Worth, Tex.,
dropped to fifth_in last year's CART standings after
winning the 1980 season championship. The winner of
at least one race in each of the last nine seasons,
Rutherford's lone 1981 victory came in the 150 mile
opener at Phoenix, Ariz. In his Milwaukee Mile outings
E

14, including the last four in a row. At the wheel of the

Milwaukee Mile. In winning the September contest,

event at Phoenix and was credited with 17th place in the
Stroh's 200 at Hampton, Ga. He also drove his Texaco
Star March-Cosworth to a fourth place finish in last
month's Indianapolis 500.

GORDON JOHNCOCK, 45, of Coldwater, Mich.,
recorded 10 top 10 finishes in 12 starts en route to
placing third in the 1981 Indy Car World Series
standings. His best showing was a second place finish in
a 500-kilometer event at Riverside Calif. Johncock
paced 29 miles in last year's Gould Rex Mays 150 but
wound up being credited with 16th place when a
gearbox problem sidelined him after 138 laps. He
returned to the Milwaukee Mile in September for the
Bettenhausen 200 and came in sixth after leading five
miles. His most prestigious victories came in the 1973
and 1982 Indianapolis 500s. He won the 1976 National
Driving Championship and is off to a strong start in
CART this year having placed fifth in the Kraco 150 at
Phoenix, Ariz., and second in a 200 mile event at
Hampton, Ga. He drives the STP Oil Treatment Wildcat-
Cosworth.

SECOND GENERATION DRIVERS
MAKING THEIR MARKS IN BOSCH/VW SUPER VEE SERIES
Many of the drivers competing in the Robert Bosch/VW Super Vee race during this weekend's Gould Rex Mays
Classic. are well on their way to becoming the Indy Car stars of the future and many familiar names will be taking to
the track for the 100-kilometer event.
In 1981, Al Unser Jr., the son of three-time Indianapolis 500 winner Al Unser, won the national championship and
both races on the Milwaukee Mile. This year's race will feature two more famous racing names, second generation
drivers who are on the threshold of stardom.

MIKE ANDRETTI
Mike Andretti, the son of former World Driving Champion Mario Andretti, is only 19, but has already become a seasoned race
driver. Mike started his racing career at age nine, when he began racing go-karts. From the start, young Andretti was a
frontrunner, winning 50 races in 75 starts.
Andretti began SCCA Formula Ford racing in 1981 and captured the Northeast Division Championship, one of the nation's
toughest areas.
The season also brought Mike's first professional experience, running three of the Bosch/VW Super Vee contests.
This year, Mike has teamed up with Arciero Racing and crew chief Pete Halsmer, who was the division's runner up in 1981.
The new association has already rendered success, as Andretti won the 1982 season opener at Phoenix International Raceway
in March, and the May event at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
He will be driving the Arciero/STP-Ralt RT5.

ROGER PENSKE, JR.
Someday, Roger Penske Jr., may very well be behind the wheel of one of his father's championship-level Indy Cars, but for
now, he divides his time between piloting race cars and furthering his education.
He began Bosch/VW Super Vee competition in 1980, running two races. The year 1981, his first full season on the circuit, was
plagued by bad luck, but punctuated by strong performances at Milwaukee in June and Michigan International Speedway in
September.
Roger drives the CAM2-Ralt RT5.

Many of the drivers competing in the Robert Bosch/VW Super Vee race during this weekend's Gould Rex Mays
Classic. are well on their way to becoming the Indy Car stars of the future and many familiar names will be taking to
In 1981, Al Unser Jr., the son of three-time Indianapolis 500 winner Al Unser, won the national championship and
both races on the Milwaukee Mile. This year's race will feature two more famous racing names, second generation
drivers who are on the threshold of stardom.
Mike Andretti, the son of former World Driving Champion Mario Andretti, is only 19, but has already become a seasoned race
driver. Mike started his racing career at age nine, when he began racing go-karts. From the start, young Andretti was a
Andretti began SCCA Formula Ford racing in 1981 and captured the Northeast Division Championship, one of the nation's
The season also brought Mike's first professional experience, running three of the Bosch/VW Super Vee contests.
This year, Mike has teamed up with Arciero Racing and crew chief Pete Halsmer, who was the division's runner up in 1981.
The new association has already rendered success, as Andretti won the 1982 season opener at Phoenix International Raceway
in March, and the May event at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
He will be driving the Arciero/STP-Ralt RT5.
Someday, Roger Penske Jr., may very well be behind the wheel of one of his father's championship-level Indy Cars, but for
now, he divides his time between piloting race cars and furthering his education.
